register_purpose: Record that three existing EXT-03 certification artifacts are defective, define precisely which of their statements are superseded, and separate contemporaneous evidence from retrospective reconstruction. This register supersedes their AUTHORITY, not their BYTES. Each subject file remains on disk byte-identical and continues to be cited as the historical record of what was certified.
non_retroactivity_clause: Nothing in this register authorizes, retroactively or otherwise, the protocol that was executed. No addendum may be read as a prelaunch authorization that did not exist. The Stage B gate passed on 2026-10-11T19:00Z, before any run; that fact is recorded, and it does not convert an invisible divergence into an authorized one.

cross_subject_findings.common_failure_mode: Each of S1, S2 and S3 certifies an artifact against a sibling artifact rather than against the frozen authority. The chain S1 -> S3 and S2 -> S1 forms a closed loop with no edge to the phase09/10 configs.
cross_subject_findings.consequence: All three certifications are mutually consistent and jointly wrong. This is why no amount of cross-checking among them could have detected the divergence.
cross_subject_findings.detection_requirement: Any future prelaunch gate must contain at least one edge that reads the frozen authority directly and compares a concrete value (optimizer name, LR, loss name, augmentation op count, channel count) - not a digest of a derived artifact.
